instruction: Configure my system so the 'python' command runs Python 3, as it's not recognized right now.

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(0.5)

metadata.explanation: Task requires setting up 'python' as an alias for 'python3' by adding it to ~/.bashrc. The evaluator checks if 'alias python=' text exists in ~/.bashrc (returns 1 if found, 0 if not). Expected result is '1\n' indicating the alias was added. This is similar in complexity to the original conda task - both involve modifying shell configuration files to make commands accessible.
metadata.verification: Verified by checking command structure: 'grep -q' performs a quiet search for 'alias python=' in ~/.bashrc. The shell expression returns 1 if pattern is found (exit code 0), 0 if not found (non-zero exit code). The exact_match metric compares this output against expected '1\n'.

llm_judge_reasons: The grep pattern 'alias python=(\")?python3(\")? *$' correctly verifies that the alias specifically points to python3, not just any alias
The evaluator semantically checks all key requirements: (1) alias exists in ~/.bashrc, (2) alias name is 'python', (3) alias target is 'python3'
The regex handles the most common cases: unquoted (alias python=python3) and double-quoted (alias python="python3") aliases

Minor limitation: The regex does not handle single quotes (alias python='python3'), though this is a less common case and doesn't affect core functionality since double-quoted and unquoted versions work correctly
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: To handle all quote styles, could update pattern to: 'alias python=(["'])?python3(["'])? *$' to also match single quotes
